scenes.label: Meet the team
scenes.title: Examples and a rule
scenes.caption: Asha compares a handwritten rule with a tiny learned predictor. In this lab, each fictional sample has two numerical features and a material label. A nearest-example method predicts from the closest labelled training examples.
scenes.dialogue: The examples can change the predictions.

scenes.label: The problem
scenes.title: Only one kind of example
scenes.caption: The first training selection contains paper examples only. A new metal-like sample is still compared with paper because the model has never been shown the other label. A model cannot gain missing coverage from a confident-looking display.
scenes.dialogue: What did we actually show it?

scenes.label: How it works
scenes.title: Keep the test separate
scenes.caption: Training examples shape the model. Held-out examples check it after the choices are made. Classification predicts categories, regression predicts numerical values and clustering groups similar examples without provided group labels. This lab uses a deliberately tiny classification method.
scenes.dialogue: Testing is not another chance to teach from the answers.

scenes.label: Your decision
scenes.title: Protect the evaluation
scenes.caption: A teammate wants to reveal test labels and copy them into training before reporting the score. Choose the action that preserves a meaningful independent check. The test examples must stay outside the training selection.
scenes.dialogue: Do we still have an unseen test?

scenes.label: What changes
scenes.title: Observe the learner
scenes.caption: The team adds the missing training label and runs the held-out examples before revealing their labels. If equally close examples disagree, this toy model asks for human review. Its result is an educational demonstration, not a reliable material detector.
scenes.dialogue: A small demonstration can show a method without proving reliability.

scenes.label: Enter the lab
scenes.title: Enter the lab
scenes.caption: Match learning tasks to methods, change the training examples and commit predictions before test labels appear. Then explain an unfamiliar result and why the held-out labels should remain outside training.
scenes.dialogue: Change the examples and watch what actually changes.
